title: Drag and Drop API browsers should not open the file if not handled

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
Moved issue from https://github.com/w3c/html/issues/1703 to here because I think it needs resolving and or clarifying.

**Overview**
I think the spec needs to explicitly state that browsers should not perform any automatic handling of dropping within a ViewPort.

**Example**
So some website use `<input type="file" />` and a user has the ability to drop a file on this element that makes sense. what does not make sense is if you slightly miss the input due to bad CSS or just miss the element the browser then opens the file making the browser act as a viewer (`file://` URI), causing the user to have to navigate back (back button, or otherwise) to the page and if they filled out a form first have the will have to refill it out as the form is cleared by the browser.

stackoverflow.com has the outlined problem.

Github.com does not so I assume they have coded handles into the pages to prevent the browser.

**Personal Views on the mater**
I think the Drag and Drop section of the specification should explicitly state that dropping a file into WebSite viewport that is not handled by Javascript or specific elements in the case of the input file should be disregarded and not acted upon.

If people wish a file to be viewed in their browser they can use the "open with" prompt of there OS or if the browsers support tabs drop it to the Tab Control area, not the viewport.

**Update**
I have created an example of some bad CSS and Javascript that can show this problem off really well. https://jsfiddle.net/qbvk506n/
The green/brown area is bad CSS and JS and the red area is the input file,
Dropping onto the green/brown area will cause the browser to redirect dropping on the red area will cause it to accept the file as a valid selection for the input.

And while i know that nobody would create such a simple example of that the same effect can be caused by other ways or a failed to implement droppable area
